name: Toralf Engan
milestone_by_age_26: Won the 1962 FIS Nordic World Ski Championships individual normal hill at Zakopane, becoming the first-ever world champion in that event, and won 22 of 26 competitions that season.
early_history_summary: Engan had his national breakthrough at age 18 when he won the junior class at Holmenkollen in 1955. He developed through the Norwegian ski jumping circuit in the late 1950s, placing second at Holmenkollen in 1960 behind Olympic champion Helmut Recknagel, before winning the Norwegian Championship in 1961 and becoming World Champion in 1962.
family_context_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources. Engan was born in Meldal Municipality, Norway, and competed for IL Leik, Hølonda club.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Norwegian ski jumping ecosystem, frontier geography, early athletic specialization, physical talent
evidence_summary: Engan emerged from Norway's dominant ski jumping tradition, achieving a national breakthrough at 18 by winning the junior class at Holmenkollen. Norway was the global frontier of ski jumping, providing him with access to world-class facilities, competitions, and a deep athletic culture. No family background information was found in reviewed sources, so family-based advantage scores remain 0. His trajectory from junior breakthrough to World Champion by 25 suggests strong physical talent and intense concentration in the sport.
starting_point: Born in Meldal Municipality, Norway in 1936; family background not documented in reviewed sources.
current_position: Retired ski jumper and former Norwegian national ski jumping coach (1967-69); settled in Trondheim with family. Now age 88.

trajectory.event: Won the junior class at Holmenkollen, marking his national breakthrough as a ski jumper.
Placed second at Holmenkollen behind Olympic champion Helmut Recknagel by a narrow margin.
Won the Norwegian Championship, his only national title.
Crowned World Champion on the normal hill at the FIS Nordic World Ski Championships in Zakopane; won 22 of 26 competitions that season; awarded the Holmenkollen Medal.
Won the Four Hills Tournament, winning three of the four competitions.
Won Olympic gold in the large hill and silver in the normal hill at the Innsbruck Winter Olympics.
Retired from competitive ski jumping after the 1966 season.

name: Yael Abecassis
milestone_by_age_26: Made her feature film debut in 'For Sasha' (1991) directed by Alexandre Arcady, appearing alongside Sophie Marceau, followed by 'Tel Aviv Stories' (1992), while also working as a fulltime TV presenter on Israel's Children's Channel.
early_history_summary: Abecassis began modeling at age 14 in the early 1980s and transitioned into television and film in the early 1990s. She appeared in two feature films by age 25 and became a fulltime presenter on Israeli children's television, building a public profile through commercials and the Castro fashion advert that made her a household name in Israel.
family_context_summary: Born in Ashkelon, Israel, to parents of Moroccan Jewish descent. Her mother, Raymonde Abecassis, was a Moroccan-Israeli singer and actress, providing early exposure to the entertainment industry.
parent_family_domain_summary: Her mother Raymonde Abecassis was a singer and actress, offering direct entertainment industry exposure and cultural fluency from a young age.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Mother in entertainment, early modeling start, Israeli TV ecosystem, physical appearance advantage
evidence_summary: Abecassis benefited from her mother Raymonde's career as a singer and actress, which provided early exposure to the entertainment world. She began modeling at 14 and leveraged this into television presenting and film roles by her early twenties. The Israeli entertainment industry in the 1990s was expanding with cable television, creating opportunities for young performers. Her early film appearances alongside major stars like Sophie Marceau suggest some industry access, though her major critical acclaim came later with Kadosh (1999) at age 32.
starting_point: Born to Moroccan Jewish parents in Ashkelon, Israel; mother Raymonde Abecassis was a singer and actress, providing early exposure to the entertainment industry.
current_position: Active Israeli actress, model, and producer; married to entrepreneur Ronny Douek; resides in Israel. Continues to appear in film and television productions.

trajectory.event: Began her modeling career as a teenager in Israel.
Made feature film debut in 'For Sasha' directed by Alexandre Arcady, appearing alongside Sophie Marceau.
Appeared in 'Tel Aviv Stories' and worked as a fulltime presenter on Israel's Children's Channel.
Starred as Rivka in Amos Gitai's critically acclaimed film 'Kadosh,' receiving favorable reviews especially in France.
Starred in the popular Israeli TV series 'Shabatot VeHagim' (Saturdays and Holidays), becoming a household name.
Starred in the acclaimed TV series 'Prisoners of War,' a role that won her a Television Academy Award.

name: Tim Cook
milestone_by_age_26: Joined IBM in 1982 at age 22 as an entry-level employee in the personal computer business after graduating from Auburn University. By age 26 he was a mid-level IBM employee with no material, independently verifiable milestone. Fame arrived at age 51 when named CEO of Apple in 2011.
early_history_summary: Cook grew up in Robertsdale, Alabama, the son of a shipyard worker and a pharmacy worker. He graduated second in his high school class, worked delivering newspapers and at a pharmacy, then attended Auburn University for industrial engineering. He joined IBM in 1982 after graduation and spent 12 years there, eventually becoming director of North American fulfillment, a role he reached well after age 26.
family_context_summary: Born in Mobile, Alabama, to Donald Cook, a shipyard worker, and Geraldine Cook, a homemaker who worked at a pharmacy. Working-class family; Cook was the first in his family to attend college.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources. Parents were a shipyard worker and a pharmacy worker with no known technology or business background.

name: Zdeňka Vávrová
milestone_by_age_26: Began working at Kleť Observatory as assistant to Antonín Mrkos in 1975 at age 30; first asteroid discoveries came in 1980 at age 35. No material milestone by age 26 found.
early_history_summary: Vávrová is a Czech astronomer who worked at Kleť Observatory for 20 years (1975-1995) as assistant to Antonín Mrkos. She is credited with discovering 115 numbered minor planets and co-discovering periodic comet 134P/Kowal-Vávrová. Her career began at age 30, well after age 26.

name: Ekta Kapoor
milestone_by_age_26: Founded Balaji Telefilms at age 18 in 1993 and had her first TV show 'Mano Ya Na Mano' picked up by Zee TV in 1995 at age 20, followed by the hit sitcom 'Hum Paanch,' establishing her as India's youngest TV producer.
early_history_summary: Kapoor started her career at age 17, interning with advertisement filmmaker Kailash Surendranath. With financing from her father, Bollywood actor Jeetendra, she founded Balaji Telefilms in 1993 at age 18. After initial failures with six rejected pilots, her first show was picked up by Zee TV in 1995, and the sitcom 'Hum Paanch' became her first hit. By 2000, her show 'Kyunki Saas Bhi Kabhi Bahu Thi' became the highest-rated Indian serial ever.
family_context_summary: Daughter of Jeetendra (born Ravi Kapoor), a major Bollywood film actor, and Shobha Kapoor, who managed the business side of Balaji Telefilms. Grew up in a wealthy entertainment industry family in Mumbai.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father Jeetendra is a legendary Bollywood actor; mother Shobha Kapoor served as managing director of Balaji Telefilms. The family's entertainment industry connections and capital directly enabled Ekta's production company.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Bollywood father, family capital, entertainment network, cable TV wave, mother as business partner, early failures as catalyst
evidence_summary: Kapoor's success was deeply enabled by her family platform: father Jeetendra's Bollywood fame provided both capital and industry credibility, while mother Shobha managed the business operations. She founded Balaji Telefilms at 18 with family financing and persevered through six rejected pilots. The Indian cable television revolution of the 1990s created a structural wave she rode to dominance. Her concentration on TV production from age 17 and direct exposure to entertainment from childhood gave her strong domain proximity. Initial failures served as a constraint-driven catalyst rather than a deterrent.
starting_point: Born to Bollywood actor Jeetendra and Shobha Kapoor in Mumbai; grew up in a wealthy entertainment industry family with direct access to film industry capital and networks.
current_position: Joint managing director and creative head of Balaji Telefilms; one of India's most influential television and film producers. Net worth estimated in hundreds of millions of dollars.

trajectory.event: Founded Balaji Telefilms with financing from her father, Bollywood actor Jeetendra.
First TV show 'Mano Ya Na Mano' picked up by Zee TV; sitcom 'Hum Paanch' became her first hit.
'Kyunki Saas Bhi Kabhi Bahu Thi' premiered on StarPlus, becoming the highest-rated Indian serial with 22.4 TRP.
Launched Balaji Motion Pictures film division; Balaji Telefilms went public.
Produced 'The Dirty Picture' and expanded Balaji's film portfolio, solidifying her position as India's TV queen.
Adapted to changing TV landscape with shows on Colors and other channels, maintaining Balaji's industry dominance.

name: Ben Feringa
milestone_by_age_26: Entered the University of Groningen in 1969 at age 18 and completed his PhD in 1978 at age 27. By age 26 he was still a PhD student with no material, independently verifiable milestone. His Nobel Prize came in 2016 at age 65.
early_history_summary: Feringa grew up on a farm in Barger-Compascuum, Netherlands, and initially wanted to be a farmer. He entered the University of Groningen in 1969 to study chemistry, fell in love with synthetic chemistry in his third year, and completed his PhD under Professor Hans Wynberg in 1978. He then worked at Shell before returning to Groningen as a professor in 1988.
family_context_summary: Son of a farmer in Barger-Compascuum, Drenthe Province, Netherlands. Grew up on a farm and initially wanted to be a farmer before becoming fascinated by chemistry.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources. Family was in farming, not chemistry or science.

name: Mohamed Bouazizi
milestone_by_age_26: Set himself on fire on December 17, 2010 in Sidi Bouzid, Tunisia, at age 26, in response to confiscation of his wares and harassment by municipal officials. His act of self-immolation triggered the Tunisian Revolution and the wider Arab Spring, leading to the downfall of President Zine al-Abidine Ben Ali.
early_history_summary: Bouazizi grew up in a poor family in Sidi Bouzid, Tunisia. After his father's death, he worked as a street vendor selling produce to support his mother, uncle, and younger siblings, earning approximately US$140 per month. He applied to join the army but was refused, and other job applications were rejected. On December 17, 2010, after municipal officials confiscated his wares and an inspector slapped him, he set himself on fire outside the governor's office, an act that sparked nationwide protests and the Arab Spring.
family_context_summary: Born into a poor family in Sidi Bouzid, a rural Tunisian town with an estimated 30% unemployment rate. His father left a three-hectare plot of land whose produce barely supported the family. After his father's death and his uncle's farm failing, Bouazizi became a street vendor to support his mother, uncle, and five siblings.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources. Family was impoverished, with no known professional or educational advantages.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Extreme poverty, institutional corruption, direct lived experience, social media amplification, Arab Spring wave
evidence_summary: Bouazizi's act was born from extreme adversity: poverty, unemployment, institutional corruption, and daily harassment as an informal street vendor. His direct lived experience of Tunisia's oppressive bureaucracy gave him an intimate understanding of the grievances shared by millions. The structural wave of social media and regional discontent amplified his individual act into a continent-wide revolution. No family, educational, or institutional advantages were documented; his impact came entirely from constraint-driven desperation that resonated globally.
starting_point: Born to a poor family in Sidi Bouzid, Tunisia; father left a small plot of land that barely sustained the family; became a street vendor as a teenager to support his mother, uncle, and five siblings.
current_position: Died on January 4, 2011 at age 26 in Ben Arous, Tunisia, from injuries sustained by self-immolation. His act triggered the Tunisian Revolution and the Arab Spring.

trajectory.event: Set himself on fire on December 17 outside the governor's office in Sidi Bouzid after municipal officials confiscated his wares and an inspector slapped him.
Died on January 4 from self-immolation injuries; his funeral drew 5,000 mourners and his act sparked the Tunisian Revolution.
The Tunisian Revolution led to the ouster of President Zine al-Abidine Ben Ali on January 14, catalyzing the wider Arab Spring across North Africa and the Middle East.

name: Brian Epstein
milestone_by_age_26: Was made a director of the family music store NEMS at age 21 in 1955 and built the record department into one of the biggest music retail outlets in Northern England. However, his significant milestone of discovering and managing the Beatles occurred in November 1961 at age 27. No material milestone by age 26 that matches the study's threshold for notable success.
early_history_summary: Epstein was born into a family of successful retailers in Liverpool. He started working at the family furniture store at 16, was made a director of NEMS at 21, and built the record department into a major retail outlet. He briefly attended RADA but left after an arrest. His transformative milestone of discovering the Beatles at the Cavern Club came in November 1961 at age 27.
family_context_summary: Born into a family of successful Jewish retailers in Liverpool. His father Harry Epstein built a furniture, appliance, and music retail business (NEMS). Brian was put in charge of the record department as a young man.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father Harry Epstein was a successful retailer who built NEMS (North End Music Stores) into a major Liverpool business. Brian was given charge of the record department, providing direct business and music industry exposure.

name: Roy Andersson
milestone_by_age_26: Directed his first feature film 'A Swedish Love Story' (filmed June-August 1969, released April 1970) at age 26, immediately after graduating from the Swedish Film Institute. The film won four prizes at the 20th Berlin International Film Festival.
early_history_summary: Andersson studied literature and philosophy at university before entering the Swedish Film Institute Film School in 1967 at age 24. He made several promising short films as a student and served as assistant director on Bo Widerberg's 'The Adalen Riots' in 1968. Immediately after graduating in 1969, he was given the opportunity to direct his first feature film, 'A Swedish Love Story,' which he shot at age 26.
family_context_summary: Born in Gothenburg (some sources say Uddevalla), Sweden. Family background not documented in reviewed sources. He studied literature and philosophy at university before entering film school.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Swedish Film Institute, Bo Widerberg mentorship, Swedish film tradition, film school facilities
evidence_summary: Andersson's early career was enabled by the Swedish Film Institute's prestigious film school, which he entered at 24. The Swedish film tradition, with directors like Ingmar Bergman and Bo Widerberg, provided a rich ecosystem. He served as assistant director to Widerberg, gaining mentorship and industry access. His student films showed promise, leading to the opportunity to direct a feature film immediately after graduation. No family background information was found in reviewed sources, so family-based scores remain 0.
starting_point: Born in Gothenburg, Sweden in 1943; studied literature and philosophy at university before entering the Swedish Film Institute Film School at age 24. Family background not documented in reviewed sources.
current_position: Active Swedish film director operating through Studio 24 in Stockholm; won the Golden Lion at Venice 2014 for 'A Pigeon Sat on a Branch Reflecting on Existence.' Continues making films in his distinctive style.

trajectory.event: Entered the Swedish Film Institute Film School; debuted with the short film 'Visiting One's Son.'
Graduated from film school and filmed his first feature 'A Swedish Love Story' between June and August.
'A Swedish Love Story' premiered at the Berlinale, winning four prizes and becoming a major critical and popular success.
Released second feature 'Giliap,' which was a financial and critical failure, leading to a 25-year break from feature filmmaking.
Founded Studio 24 production company to make films with total creative freedom.
'Songs from the Second Floor' won the Cannes Film Festival Jury Prize.
'A Pigeon Sat on a Branch Reflecting on Existence' won the Golden Lion at the Venice International Film Festival.

name: Manu Chao
milestone_by_age_26: Released a demo with Hot Pants in 1984 at age 23 that gained local critical praise but little attention, and a first album in 1986 at age 25. Founded Mano Negra in 1987 at age 26, but the band's significant success came with the debut LP 'Patchanka' in 1988 at age 27, scoring the French indie hit 'Mala Vida.' No material milestone by age 26 found.
early_history_summary: Chao began his musical career in Paris, busking and playing with groups such as Hot Pants and Los Carayos in the mid-1980s. Hot Pants released a demo in 1984 and an album in 1986 with limited success. He founded Mano Negra with his brother and cousin in 1987, but the band's breakthrough came with their debut LP in 1988. His solo career breakthrough came even later with 'Clandestino' in 1998.
family_context_summary: Born to Galician and Basque parents with partly Cuban roots in Paris. His brother Antoine Chao is also a musician (trumpeter), and his cousin Santiago Casariego was a drummer. The three founded Mano Negra together.
parent_family_domain_summary: Family of Galician, Basque, and Cuban heritage; brother Antoine and cousin Santiago were musical collaborators in Mano Negra, suggesting a family culture of musical engagement.

name: Heidi Løke
milestone_by_age_26: Won the EHF EURO 2008 gold medal with Norway's national handball team on December 14, 2008, two days after her 26th birthday, marking her first major international title and the start of a dominant career.
early_history_summary: Løke began playing handball at age 10 but was a late bloomer who only got serious about the sport at 18. She played for IL Runar until 2000, then moved to Larvik HK where she was a fourth-choice and played on the B-team. She transferred to Gjerpen IF in 2002 for more playing time, made her first national team appearance at 24 in 2006, and after a stint in Denmark with Aalborg DH, returned to Larvik where her career took off with the EHF EURO 2008 gold.
family_context_summary: Born in Tønsberg, Norway, and grew up in Sandefjord as one of seven siblings. Four of her siblings play handball, most notably her older brother Frank Løke, who is a fixture on Norway's national team and considered one of the world's best male line players. Her sister Lise also played handball at Gjerpen.
parent_family_domain_summary: A deep handball family: brother Frank Løke is a Norwegian national team player and one of the world's best male line players. Multiple siblings play handball, creating a family culture of training and competition.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Norwegian handball ecosystem, handball family, brother Frank Løke, late bloomer, extreme training dedication, Toppidrettsgymnaset
evidence_summary: Løke grew up in Norway, the global frontier of women's handball, in a family where four siblings played the sport, including brother Frank Løke, a national team star. She attended Toppidrettsgymnaset (an elite sports academy) in Sandefjord and had access to Norway's world-class handball pipeline. Despite being described as 'not a standout talent' and a 'late bloomer' who was fourth-choice at Larvik, she developed extraordinary training dedication (~1000 hours/year) and eventually broke through at 26. Her adversity as an overlooked player served as a catalyst for her intense work ethic.
starting_point: Born in Tønsberg, Norway in 1982; grew up in Sandefjord as one of seven children in a handball family; brother Frank Løke is a Norwegian national team handball star.
current_position: Retired from playing in 2025; serves as handball coach for the women's team at IL Runar and as assistant coach for the Poland national team.

trajectory.event: Joined Larvik HK from IL Runar but was fourth-choice line player and spent time on the B-team in the second division.
Transferred to Gjerpen IF for more playing time under coach Leif Gautestad.
Made her first appearance for the Norwegian national team, though she would not play again for two years.
Won her first EHF EURO gold medal with Norway on December 14, two days after her 26th birthday, launching her international medal streak.
Won EHF Champions League with Larvik HK and was named IHF World Player of the Year.
Won Olympic gold medal with Norway at the London Summer Olympics.
Won her third EHF EURO gold medal with Norway while playing for Győri ETO KC in Hungary.
Won her fourth EHF EURO gold medal, capping a career with 226 national team appearances and 801 goals.

name: Svetislav Pešić
milestone_by_age_26: Played for KK Partizan (1967-1971, ages 18-22) as a decent but not star shooting guard, then moved to KK Bosna Sarajevo (1971-1979). His major playing achievements — Yugoslav League champion (1978) and EuroLeague champion (1979) — came at ages 29-30. No material milestone by age 26 found.
early_history_summary: Pešić was born in Novi Sad but grew up in Pirot, Serbia. He started as a football goalkeeper before switching to basketball. He played for KK Pirot, then signed for Partizan in 1967 at age 18, where he played four years as a decent but non-star player. He moved to KK Bosna Sarajevo in 1971 under coach Bogdan Tanjević, helping the team rise from the second division, but his major titles came in 1978-79 at ages 29-30. His coaching career began in 1982 at age 33.
family_context_summary: Born in Novi Sad, Serbia (then part of Yugoslavia). Grew up in Pirot, a city near the Bulgarian border. Family background not documented in reviewed sources.
